name: Punk fashion
summary: The dress of the London punk scene from 1976. It has ripped and pinned T-shirts, tartan bondage trousers, studded leather jackets, rubber and PVC, and safety pins as ornament.

philosophy.core_thesis: Dress is a protest that the wearer makes by hand: the garment is torn, pinned and written on, and it shocks on purpose.
design_principles: Tear, slash or cut open the cloth, and pin or lace the opening shut with a safety pin or a cord.
Print a slogan or an image on a plain cotton T-shirt by screen print, in one or two flat colours.
Cut the trouser narrow, to 16 to 18 cm at the hem, and join the legs with a bondage strap.
Use black leather, tartan, PVC and rubber as the main cloths.
Fix 20 or more metal studs or spikes along the collar and the shoulder of a leather jacket.
Hold the look with chains, zips, safety pins and dog collars.
Make or modify the piece yourself, and keep each stitch and tear visible.
anti_patterns: Soft floral prints and flowing cloth

silhouette.shape: A narrow, hard column: tight trousers or a short skirt, a cropped jacket and heavy boots, with chains and straps added.
silhouette.line: A narrow shoulder, a short jacket at the hip, and a trouser leg that is slim to the ankle.
silhouette.fit: Close to the body in the leg, with the top left torn, loose or cropped.
silhouette.proportion: Trouser hem 16 to 18 cm; jacket length to the hip; boot shaft 20 cm; safety pins 3 to 5 cm along the tear.
rules: Keep the leg narrow and the boot heavy.
Crop the jacket at the hip and stud the shoulder.
Tear the top at the neck or the hem, then pin it.
Hang a chain from the belt loop to the pocket.

fabrics.rule: Choose a hard, cheap or shocking cloth: black leather, tartan, plain cotton jersey, PVC and rubber, with steel studs and pins.

methods: bondage straps and zips sewn across the leg
studs and spikes fixed to the leather
construction.closures: Zips, safety pins, buckles and straps; a leather jacket closes with a diagonal zip.
construction.details: A cropped biker jacket with studs, bondage straps between the knees, a chain at the hip, a tartan kilt and a dog collar.

surface.pattern: Tartan check, hand-painted or screen-printed slogans, and ripped and pinned areas.
surface.gloss: Leather at 15–30 GU; PVC at 60–90 GU; cotton and tartan at 2–5 GU.
surface.wear: The style wants wear and damage: a torn hem, a faded print and a scuffed leather.

palette.strategy: Black as the base, with red tartan and one hard accent: hot pink or acid yellow.

making.scale: A boutique in King's Road and the wearer's own hand; a few small runs, then a mass of cheap copies from 1977.
making.signs: Hand-fixed studs and pins, torn edges, uneven print and a patched or mended hem.

pieces.form: Cropped biker jacket with a diagonal zip and studs
Cotton T-shirt with a slogan and a tear at the neck
Narrow tartan trousers with a bondage strap
Narrow jeans with rips and pins
Short tight PVC skirt with a zip

canonical_works.maker: Vivienne Westwood, Malcolm McLaren and Jamie Reid

emotion.target_response: A jolt of anger and speed: the viewer sees a hard, damaged and defiant look that wants to be noticed.

use_cases: a costume brief for a 1970s punk film
a stage costume for a rock show
a study note on subculture dress
avoid_when: the brief wants a refined, formal or luxury look
the brief wants a soft, romantic or natural dress
the brief needs a corporate uniform

modifiers.how: Keep the tartan and the narrow cut, cut it clean in wool, and drop the tears and the pins.
Keep the screen print and denim, drop the chains and the studs, and wear a hoodie.
